title: Introduce differential linguistic-coverage reconciler and CI guard for prompt-sets
author: Aisha Malik
description: Summary: Adds a CI hook and orchestration component that computes a differential linguistic coverage score between new and baseline prompt-sets and enforces a soft-fail gate when coverage delta exceeds thresholds. Motivation: Some recent regressions were triggered by distributional shifts in token-level morphology and named-entity coverage across prompt cohorts; numerical metrics missed these because they aggregated at a semantic level. This PR introduces a reconciler that: (1) computes n-gram and morphological span coverage over prompt-sets, (2) aligns tokenization-robust shards between runs, (3) produces a compact coverage diff and an explainable report with top divergent spans, and (4) plugs into CI to fail builds when the differential coverage exceeds configurable sensitivity tiers. Checklist: - [x] Implement reconciler core and exporter - [x] Add unit tests for tokenization aligner and diff heuristics - [x] Add CI hook integration + smoke test in eval pipeline - [x] Add documentation and runbook entry - [x] Add Linear links and changelog entry Changes in this PR: commits: see commit_summaries field; major files changed listed in changed_files. How it works: The reconciler ingests two serialized prompt-set snapshots (baseline and candidate), canonicalizes tokenization using a configurable token normalizer (handles whitespace/punctuation variants, Unicode normalization, and optional subword collapse), extracts span-level identifiers (n-grams up to 4, morphological lemma signatures, named-entity markers), and computes coverage histograms. We then compute a differential coverage vector and summary metrics: overall coverage delta, uncovered-top-k, and span-frequency-shift. The CI hook executes on PRs that touch prompt-sets or eval configs; it runs a small sampled evaluation (configurable sample size) and rejects the PR if the sensitivity tier is triggered. Sensitivity tiers: - low: informational, annotate PR - medium: soft-fail with reviewer override - high: hard-fail (CI blocks merge) Backwards compatibility: The reconciler is opt-in via eval_config coverage_reconciler block; default behaviour is off to avoid unexpected CI failures for legacy repos. Docs and runbook: Added docs/eval/linguistic_reconciler.md and runbooks/coverage_reconciler.md with examples and remediation suggestions (e.g., tokenization aliases, cohort splitting). Runtime characteristics: The reconciler is optimized for incremental snapshots and runs in ~30-90s on typical prompt-set sizes (1k-5k examples) when sampling tier is medium. We included a caching layer keyed on prompt-set fingerprint to avoid repeated full recomputes. Runtime tests included cache hit/miss scenarios and a stress run against a 50k prompt-set sample. Rollout plan: - Merge to main behind feature flag - Enable low sensitivity on nightly smoke runs for 2 weeks - Enable medium sensitivity for PRs touching eval configs for a month and gather false positives - Consider default medium sensitivity after stabilization Related work and references: ENG-1428 (coverage regressions post-tokenizer-update), ENG-1439 (prompt-set drift detection design).

release_notes: Introduce optional linguistic coverage reconciler for prompt-sets and a CI hook that can soft/hard fail PRs based on differential coverage. Opt-in via eval_config.coverage_reconciler. Provides explainable span-level diffs and normalization previews.
